subject: Clarifying DPA responsibilities, subprocessors, and breach notice timeline
messages:
From: Caroline Miles <caroline.miles@medsys.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medsys.health>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA & data handling after today's demo

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the demo today, it was helpful to see the Dedicated runtime in action. Before we move forward with a pilot, our InfoSec and Privacy teams asked me to capture a few clarifications so they can sign off on a short-form DPA and a scoping memo: 

1) Controller vs Processor: We want to confirm whether MedSys or Redwood is considered the controller for patient identifiers that are uploaded for model inference in the pilot. Our legal says that if Redwood is a processor, we need the DPA to state that explicitly and to include the specific permitted processing activities.

2) Subprocessors: Please provide a current list of subprocessors (cloud providers, analytics tools, monitoring). If you use any third-party logging or observability providers that store tokenized text, we need to know who and where.

3) Data retention & logging: We need defaults and configuration options for request/response retention, KV cache retention, and audit/log export windows. Our default requirement is 90 days for inference logs, but we can consider shorter windows if they are configurable and auditable.

4) PII handling & redaction: Can Redwood configure automatic redaction or token masking at ingest? If not, we need to document the recommended customer-side approach and any built-in safeguards.

5) Breach notice: What is Redwood's committed notification timeframe for security incidents that affect MedSys data? SOC-2 language typically references "as soon as reasonably practicable" but we prefer an explicit window (e.g., 72 hours) for incidents materially affecting PHI.

If you could send a short written response with attachments (DPA excerpt, subprocessors list, and an example audit log csv), that would speed up our internal review. Also looping Raj (product) who will own the pilot.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up if that is easier.

— Caroline
Caroline Miles
Director, Privacy & Compliance
MedSys Health
caroline.miles@medsys.health
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Caroline Miles <caroline.miles@medsys.health>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medsys.health>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA & data handling after today's demo

Hi Caroline —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers below and I'll attach supporting artifacts in a follow-up: 

1) Controller/Processor: For typical inference-only pilots, MedSys is the controller of the data you upload; Redwood acts as a processor. We can add explicit permitted processing activities into the DPA excerpt (attached: redwood-dpa-v1.3.pdf) to reflect inference, optional caching, and metrics collection.

2) Subprocessors: We maintain a current subprocessors registry (cloud infra + monitoring + alerting). I don't have the canonical list in this mailbox right now — looping Neha from SE who will drop the latest subprocessors CSV and brief notes about where text is stored.

3) Retention & logging: By default hosted logs are retained 30 days; Dedicated allows configurable retention down to 0 days (no logs) or up to 365 days. For pilot we can set inference logs to 30 days but provide an export of audit records on-demand. I'll include the retention configuration doc.

4) PII handling: Redwood doesn't perform automatic heuristic redaction by default. We offer token-level masking hooks and customer-side SDK guidance to scrub PII at ingest. There is also an option for a pre-ingest redact plugin for Dedicated customers; Neha will share the integration notes.

5) Breach notice: Our standard DPA commits to "prompt" notification and detailed incident support. We recognize your preference for an explicit window; Laura (legal) is on copy and will confirm whether we can accept a 72-hour notification SLA for incidents impacting customer data.

Next steps I propose: 
- Neha to share subprocessors list + integration notes (today).
- Laura to confirm breach notification language (tomorrow).
- Ben to send DPA excerpt + sample audit log (by EOD tomorrow).

If helpful, let's schedule a 30-min call early next week to finalize scoping and sign-off path.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood-dpa-v1.3.pdf (DPA excerpt, redacted for public sharing)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Caroline Miles <caroline.miles@medsys.health>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA & data handling after today's demo

Caroline —

Thanks for the detailed list. I wanted to clarify a couple of legal points so you have a clear record: 

- Controller vs Processor: As Ben noted, for the pilot where MedSys uploads patient identifiers strictly for inference, MedSys will be identified as the controller and Redwood as processor. We'll add an explicit section to the DPA that enumerates the processing activities (ingest, inference, optional KV cache, logging for operational and security purposes).

- Subprocessors: Our subprocessors registry includes (examples): AWS (us-east-1) for compute/storage, Sentry for error telemetry (no raw prompt storage), Datadog for metrics (aggregated). We can provide a signed subprocessors appendix and indicate which subprocessors (if any) may have access to token-level logs in Dedicated. We'll provide the full list in CSV as requested.

- Breach notice: We're open to committing to a 72-hour initial notification for incidents that materially affect customer data confidentiality or integrity, subject to the caveat that the initial notice may be preliminary and followed by a full incident report once investigations are complete. We will include that in the DPA addendum.

- Retention: For Dedicated pilots, we'll document configuration controls and an audit path for retention changes. For any retention shorter than 14 days we request written confirmation of the consequences for debugging and support (e.g., potential loss of traceability).

Please note: any obligation requiring on-demand access to raw token-level logs by MedSys will require an operational runbook to be agreed (how we query, export format, safeguards). Happy to draft that runbook outline for review.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medsys.health>

Thanks Ben/Laura — helpful. A few quick asks from product/ops: 

- Can you share an example audit log csv (fields + a 7-row sample) so our engineering team can validate ingestion?
- For the pilot timeline, we want to scope a 6-week PoC: week 1 integration, week 2 pilot dataset loading, weeks 3-5 evaluation, week 6 wrap/decision. Does that align with Redwood's typical pilot support?
- Also, pricing thought — for the PoC we'd prefer a capped usage commitment rather than pay-as-you-go. Who on your team handles PoC commercial terms?

Happy to align on a short call if needed.

— Raj
Raj Patel
Senior Product Manager, MedSys Health
